- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts show gradual upward drift (increasing trend) while true prices often exhibit sharp drops or mean-reversion after spikes.
- After a price spike (e.g., >85), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly — overestimates subsequent days.
- Model underestimates true price volatility — fails to capture sharp downward corrections or sudden spikes.
- Forecasts are too smooth; lack of noise or sharp transitions in true price data is not reflected.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices, especially when history includes recent high values.
- Model does not adjust for mean reversion — continues to trend upward even when true prices show downward correction.
- Forecasts often lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in downward corrections.
- Model overconfident in upward trend — fails to anticipate sudden drops or corrections in mid-to-late forecast horizon.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 2–5% after a spike, and smoothed to match true volatility patterns.
